benefitsData.title: Benefits of Chemical Skin Peels
benefitsData.description: A chemical peel treatment offers a range of benefits, improving both skin health and appearance. From exfoliation to collagen production, this skin rejuvenation procedure helps achieve a radiant, youthful glow:

component.title: 1. Deep Exfoliation:
component.description: Removes dead skin cells, unclogs pores, and promotes skin cell turnover for a smoother texture and glowing skin.

component.title: 2. Even Skin Tone & Brightness:
component.description: Reduces hyperpigmentation, dark spots, and sun damage, giving you a brighter, even-toned complexion.

component.title: 3. Boosted Collagen Production:
component.description: Stimulates collagen and elastin for firmer, youthful skin, reducing fine lines and wrinkles.

component.title: 4. Minimized Pores & Clearer Skin:
component.description: Refines enlarged pores, controls acne breakouts, and improves skin texture for a flawless look.

component.title: 5. Fast & Visible Results:
component.description: Most people see skin brightening and improved texture within days to weeks, making it a quick skin rejuvenation solution.

extraFields.detail1:
What to Expect During a Chemical Peel

A chemical peel treatment is a multi-step process designed to enhance skin rejuvenation and improve skin texture. Here's what happens during the procedure:

1. Consultation & Skin Analysis:Before treatment, a skincare specialist will assess your skin type and concerns such as hyperpigmentation, acne scars, or fine lines to determine the most effective chemical peel for you.

2. Application Process:During the procedure:

3. Neutralization & Post-Treatment Care:

​

The skin is cleansed to remove oils and impurities.

A chemical solution (such as glycolic acid, TCA, or lactic acid) is applied for a set time.

You may feel a tingling or mild burning sensation, which is normal.

​

The peeling solution is neutralized and removed.

Your skin is moisturized to soothe any redness or irritation.

You'll receive aftercare instructions for optimal healing and glowing skin results.
extraFields.detail2:
Aftercare and Recovery Tips

Proper post-peel skincare is crucial for achieving radiant, youthful skin and preventing irritation:

1. Hydration & Moisturization:Apply a gentle moisturizer to support skin healing and prevent dryness.

2. Sun Protection is a Must:Use broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30+) daily to shield sensitive skin from UV damage and prevent hyperpigmentation.

3. Avoid Picking or Peeling:Resist the urge to touch or peel flaking skin it can lead to scarring and irritation.

4. Use Gentle Skincare Products:Stick to mild cleansers and avoid harsh exfoliants, retinoids, or AHAs until your skin fully heals.

faq.question: How long do chemical peel results last?
faq.answer: Duration varies by peel depth. Superficial peels typically require repeat sessions to maintain improvement. Medium peels can produce results lasting several months. Deep peels produce longer-lasting skin texture improvements; however, results depend on the individual's skin, sun exposure habits and aftercare compliance. The clinical team will discuss realistic expectations at your consultation.

faq.question: Can I apply makeup after a chemical peel?
faq.answer: Wait at least 24 to 48 hours before applying any makeup following a superficial peel. For medium or deep peels, the recovery period is longer and your specialist will provide specific guidance on when it is safe to resume makeup use. Applying products too soon can irritate healing skin.

faq.question: Are chemical peels painful?
faq.answer: Superficial and medium peels typically produce a mild tingling or temporary burning sensation during application, which settles quickly. Deeper peels may require topical numbing and involve more post-procedure discomfort. The clinical team explains what to expect before the procedure begins.

faq.question: How many sessions will I need?
faq.answer: Superficial peels are often performed in a planned series of sessions spaced several weeks apart to achieve gradual improvement. Medium and deep peels typically address the target concerns in one or two treatments. The number of sessions required depends on your skin concerns, peel type and how your skin responds.

faq.question: Are there any side effects or risks?
faq.answer: Common side effects include redness, peeling, mild irritation and temporary skin sensitivity, particularly in the days following the procedure. Deeper peels involve a longer healing period. All chemical peels carry risks including post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, particularly in darker skin tones, and potential for infection if aftercare guidance is not followed. These risks are discussed fully during your consultation.

metadata.overviewData:
Chemical Peel Treatment at Ryan Clinic, Delhi

Chemical skin peels are a dermatological procedure in which a chemical solution is applied to the skin surface to accelerate exfoliation and promote the renewal of skin cells. The depth of the peel — superficial, medium or deep — is selected based on the patient's skin concerns, skin type and assessment findings.

At Ryan Clinic in Delhi, chemical peel treatments are advised following an individual skin assessment. This helps determine whether a peel is appropriate, which peel type is most suitable and what preparation and aftercare the patient requires.

What Is a Chemical Skin Peel?

A chemical peel uses a carefully selected acidic solution applied to the skin for a defined period. This controlled exfoliation encourages the removal of damaged outer skin layers and supports the skin's natural renewal process. The result, over time, can include improved skin texture, more even skin tone and reduced appearance of surface-level pigmentation or acne marks.

How Do Chemical Skin Peels Work?

The solution disrupts the bonds holding dead skin cells together, triggering controlled shedding and stimulating collagen production in the deeper skin layers. The depth of effect depends on the type and concentration of the agent used and the duration of application.

Is a Chemical Peel Right for You?

Chemical peels are not suitable for every patient. They are generally not recommended for patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding, those with a history of keloid scarring, individuals currently using isotretinoin, or those with active skin infections or open eczema. A clinical consultation is required to confirm suitability.

typesData.details:
Types of Chemical Skin Peels

Chemical peels are categorised by depth of penetration. The appropriate peel type is determined during your clinical skin assessment at Ryan Clinic.

1. Superficial Peels

Superficial peels use alpha-hydroxy acids (AHAs) such as glycolic acid or lactic acid, or low-concentration beta-hydroxy acids. They target the outermost skin layer, require minimal downtime and are often used in a series of treatments for gradual improvement of skin texture and mild pigmentation concerns.

2. Medium Peels

Medium-depth peels use trichloroacetic acid (TCA) and penetrate into the outer middle layers of the skin. Patients typically experience several days of visible peeling following the procedure. They address moderate pigmentation, acne scarring and uneven skin texture more extensively than superficial peels.

3. Deep Peels

Deep peels use phenol or high-strength TCA and penetrate more deeply into the skin. They provide substantial skin remodelling and prolonged improvement in skin texture, though they carry a longer recovery period and require careful patient selection. Deep peels are not appropriate for all skin types; suitability is assessed during consultation. Results are long-lasting but do not prevent the future effects of sun exposure, ageing or subsequent skin conditions.
